note: Two roots per context-card page, five previews on each side. context-card: the open card's floating layer, a client-only state the sketches (tools/geist/sketch/context-card.*.json) render on the mirror and the census page opens through the prepare script — the reference shows the card open in previews 4 and 5 only, so ours pins exactly those eight. context-card-trigger: the wrapper around the slotted content, present on all seventeen cards, read on `.trigger`. Run each side with theme light and dark; width fixes every preview at the mirror's 600px stage. The card's own box is moved and sized by inline styles on both sides, so its position is not compared; the text-bearing parts are read as soft. The card's width and height are set inline from the measured content, so they follow the text in our font: `card` and `fade` are named as text parts, like `box` and `body`. Both sides must be read at the SAME viewport — the layer is fixed to the viewport, so its width is the window's; the mirror pane defaults narrow, and reading it at 426px against ours at 1367px reported 208 differences that were only the window size. Resize both to 1367x924 before running. The prepare script scrolls each group into view BEFORE opening it: placement flips to the side with room, measured at open time, so a group below the fold resolves every card to `top` and the reference's four sides collapse to one. The card's `transform` is read as soft: on the mirror it is the sketch's static value, because the mirror strips scripts and nothing recomputes placement — every reference card sits 425-541px above its trigger, which no live run would produce. Ours is computed live and correct against its trigger (top 29 above, bottom 75 below, left 327 left, right 53 right). The SIDE each card resolves to is the real check, and all four now match.
